subject: Interim goodwill rate adjustment for QA blocker - NovaHealth
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novahealth.com>, procure-nova@novahealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Interim goodwill rate adjustment for QA blocker - NovaHealth

Team —

Quick background: NovaHealth (DH-8843) hit a last-mile QA blocker on Friday after our prefetch change caused flaky validation for one of their heavy embedding routes. Their launch was delayed and they are asking for a temporary commercial accommodation while we deliver the patch. Sara included a short error log (attached).

What I need from this thread: a recommended commercial remedy we can propose to NovaHealth today so they can move procurement forward. The customer wants something in-hand before signature. Key constraints:
- Engineering estimate for a hotfix and rollout: Marcus, can you confirm ETA?
- Commercial ask from customer: one-time credit + temporary overage rate reduction for the first 8 weeks. Sara suggests a modest credit to offset onboarding costs.
- We need an exec-level signoff (Marissa) if credit > $25k.

My preliminary proposal (please critique):
- One-time goodwill credit: $30,000
- Temporary overage rate: 25% discount on overage for 8 weeks post-launch
- Contingency: credit void if customer extends beyond agreed launch window or if issue is caused by their integration.

Attachments: novahealth_qa_error_log.pdf and provisional_credit_calc.xlsx — the calc tab has two scenarios (25k and 40k).

Marcus — can you confirm hotfix ETA and any residual risk? Aditya/Laura/Karthik — please weigh in on the commercial numbers and approval path.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe@redwood.com

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 09:22 AM Chloe Martin <chloe@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick background: NovaHealth (DH-8843) hit a last-mile QA blocker on Friday after our prefetch change caused flaky validation for one of their heavy embedding routes.

Chloe — short answer on ETA: I can get a targeted hotfix out in 3 business days (Friday EOD PT) assuming CI passes and we don't hit downstream infra contention. Rollout to prod can be staged over the weekend. Risk: if their dataset triggers a different code path we may need another patch (low probability, ~10%).

Technical ask for product: this was caused by our sequence padding in the prefetch flow combined with an edge-case in their payload. I've logged a follow-up to make the prefetch validation more defensive; that work is Scope+ and will land in the next sprint (2 weeks). The hotfix I described is a quick guard.

From a support perspective, I recommend limited commercial relief tied to the hotfix window (8 weeks) rather than an open-ended concession.

Marcus
Marcus Lin

marcus@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interim goodwill rate adjustment for QA blocker - NovaHealth

Thanks Marcus and Chloe — solid context. Commercial suggestion from my side:

Proposal A (conservative):
- $20,000 one-time goodwill credit
- 20% overage discount for 6 weeks after launch
- Formal CLA/workback signed by customer that we will be able to monitor load patterns

Proposal B (move fast / keep deal):
- $35,000 one-time credit (contingent approval)
- 30% overage discount for 8 weeks
- Acceptance: legal review + DocuSign amendment to existing SOW

If we go with B, we should request an executive sign-off (Marissa) and loop in legal for the amendment. Also suggest we hold back 25% of the credit until post-launch smoke test completes.

Commercial rationale: NovaHealth is a mid-size strategic customer in healthcare; the ARR upside and reference value outweigh a modest one-time concession.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Interim goodwill rate adjustment for QA blocker - NovaHealth

Thanks — I ran the numbers with finance. Quick points:
- Finance will greenlight up to $25k in unilateral goodwill without an exec exception. Anything > $25k needs VP-level sign-off.
- If we offer a temporary overage discount, it should be tied to volume caps to avoid open exposure (recommend cap = 1.5x their current monthly committed tokens for the 8-week window).
- Legal will need a short amendment with a clause that credit is non-recoupable and conditional on our hotfix timeline.

Marissa — can you weigh in on making an exception to the $25k threshold? If you prefer, we can present 2 options to NovaHealth: (1) faster signature + $25k + 25% discount, or (2) $35k + 30% discount with exec sign-off and DocuSign amendment.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clear options. My decision:
- Approve a one-time goodwill credit of $30,000 (conditional).
- Approve a 28% overage discount for 8 weeks, capped at 1.5x current committed tokens.
- Holdback: 30% of the credit until post-launch smoke test passes (confirmed by Marcus).

Conditions:
1) Legal to prepare short DocuSign amendment (Laura / Aditya, please coordinate) — amendment must include the cap, holdback, and a clause limiting credit to issues caused by Redwood.
2) Customer must sign amendment before credit is applied. Procurement contact included in thread.
3) Marcus to confirm hotfix rollout and smoke-test window; once smoke test passes we release holdback.

Chloe — please communicate the approved option to NovaHealth as a firm offer and attach the DocuSign link once legal has prepared it. Laura — lead on the amendment; Aditya — coordinate with finance to schedule credit timing once the amendment is executed.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
